text:
The change adds a static null0 route for 172.16.2.0/24 on PAO and PIT, which are likely border routers redistributing into the peers. cust2's prefix is 172.16.2.0/24, so a null route on PAO and PIT could blackhole cust2 traffic if the static route wins over the OSPF/BGP-learned route. Administrative distance for a static route is 1, which beats OSPF (110), so cust2 traffic transiting PAO/PIT could be dropped. I'll test for that regression and for unchanged behavior elsewhere.
